svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Fungal hyphae: two types."], [1, "Septate hyphae: cross-walls (septa) divide the hypha; pores let cytoplasm and nuclei pass."], [5, "Aseptate (coenocytic) hyphae: no cross-walls; one continuous cytoplasm with many nuclei."], [9, "Both grow at the tip, where vesicles bring new wall and membrane."]]
svg.title: Septate and aseptate hyphae
svg.desc: A septate fungal hypha with cross-walls and pores and one or two nuclei per compartment, compared with an aseptate hypha with many nuclei in continuous cytoplasm; both growing at the tip.
svg.text: Longitudinal sections; wall shown thick for clarity.
e.g. Penicillium, mushrooms; one or two nuclei per compartment

g.data-info: Fungal hyphae have walls of chitin, not cellulose.
Divides a septate hypha into compartments. A pore in the middle lets cytoplasm, organelles and usually nuclei move through.
Septate hyphae usually have one or two nuclei per compartment; aseptate hyphae have many nuclei in one continuous cytoplasm.
Older parts of the hypha are more vacuolated.
Cytoplasm streams along the hypha towards the growing tip.
Hyphae grow only at the tip, where vesicles add new wall and membrane.

g.text: e.g. Rhizopus (bread mould); many nuclei, continuous cytoplasm
Both grow only at the tip; cytoplasm streams towards it
